quizzes.title: Unit 1 Assessment — Texas Foundations: Identity, Freedom, and Geography
quizzes.description: This quiz has 12 multiple-choice questions about Unit 1. Choose the best answer for each question. You have 2 tries, and your higher score counts.

questions.text: A diary written by a Texas settler in 1836 is an example of a...

answers.text: primary source
secondary source
map legend
cultural region

questions.text: Which of these is a SECONDARY source?

answers.text: A letter written by Stephen F. Austin
A photograph taken in 1901
A textbook chapter written today about the Texas Revolution
A hand-drawn map from 1840

questions.text: What is the FIRST thing a good historian does when studying a source?

answers.text: Decide whether they like it
Observe and describe what they actually see
Throw out anything confusing
Write the conclusion

questions.text: Why should historians ask cautionary questions about a source?

answers.text: To prove the source is useless
Because a source might leave things out or show only one point of view
Because primary sources are always wrong
To make the work take longer

questions.text: What does the Declaration of Independence explain?

answers.text: Why people have the right to govern themselves and to break from an unfair government
How to build roads
The names of all Texas counties
How to elect a governor of Texas

questions.text: What does the Bill of Rights do?

answers.text: Creates the three branches of government
Protects individual freedoms, like speech and religion
Lists the four regions of Texas
Sets the price of goods

questions.text: What does "consent of the governed" mean?

answers.text: The king decides everything.
Government gets its power from the agreement of the people.
Only soldiers can vote.
Laws do not apply to leaders.

questions.text: Which list names the four physical regions of Texas?

answers.text: Gulf, Plains, Puebloan, Southeastern
Coastal Plains, North Central Plains, Great Plains, Mountains and Basins
Panhandle, Hill Country, Piney Woods, Big Bend
North, South, East, West

questions.text: Which region is the largest and has the most people?

answers.text: Coastal Plains
North Central Plains
Great Plains
Mountains and Basins

questions.text: Which region is the smallest and driest, in far west Texas?

answers.text: Coastal Plains
North Central Plains
Great Plains
Mountains and Basins

questions.text: What does a map legend (or key) do?

answers.text: Shows which direction is north
Explains what the colors and symbols on the map mean
Tells who drew the map
Measures the temperature

questions.text: Why did many early Texas settlements grow near rivers?

answers.text: Rivers kept people away from farms.
Rivers provided water for drinking and farming, and a way to travel and trade.
Rivers were the only places with mountains.
The law required it.

quizzes.title: Unit 2 Assessment — Indigenous Texas Before and Today
quizzes.description: This quiz has 12 multiple-choice questions about Unit 2. Choose the best answer for each question. You have 2 tries, and your higher score counts.

questions.text: Which list names the four cultural regions of American Indian groups in Texas?

answers.text: Gulf, Plains, Puebloan, and Southeastern
Coastal Plains, North Central Plains, Great Plains, and Mountains and Basins
Spanish, Mexican, Republic, and State
North, South, East, and West

questions.text: What shaped the four cultural regions of Texas?

answers.text: Spanish laws
Geography: land, climate, water, plants, and animals
Railroads
The Texas Constitution

questions.text: Which cultural region had marshes, bays, and plentiful seafood?

answers.text: Gulf
Plains
Puebloan
Southeastern

questions.text: Which group lived along the Gulf Coast?

answers.text: Caddo
Karankawa
Lipan Apache
Jumano

questions.text: Why were the Lipan Apache nomadic?

answers.text: They disliked staying in one place.
They followed the bison herds on the Plains, which were their main source of food and supplies.
They were forced to move by the railroad.
They were traders who lived on ships.

questions.text: What made the Caddo different from the Lipan Apache?

answers.text: The Caddo farmed in permanent villages in the Southeastern forests.
The Caddo followed bison herds across the Plains.
The Caddo lived only on the Gulf Coast.
The Caddo did not grow any crops.

questions.text: The Caddo grew corn, beans, and squash together. What were these crops called?

answers.text: The Cattle Trail
The Three Sisters
The Lone Star crops
The Gulf harvest

questions.text: The Jumano are best known as...

answers.text: builders of the Alamo
long-distance traders who connected groups across hundreds of miles
ranchers in the Panhandle
Spanish missionaries

questions.text: What does "barter" mean?

answers.text: Trading goods directly for other goods, without money
Building a mound village
Hunting bison
Writing a treaty

questions.text: Which Indigenous community is located near El Paso in far west Texas?

answers.text: Alabama-Coushatta Tribe
Kickapoo Traditional Tribe
Ysleta del Sur Pueblo
Karankawa

questions.text: How did the Caddo and the Comanche govern themselves?

answers.text: Both had a king chosen by Spain.
The settled Caddo formed a confederacy with councils; the mobile Comanche used flexible band leadership.
Neither group had any leaders.
Both used the Texas Legislature.

questions.text: Why is it important to study American Indian peoples as living communities, not only as people of the past?

answers.text: Because they all moved away from Texas
Because nations like the Alabama-Coushatta, Kickapoo, and Ysleta del Sur Pueblo live in Texas today with their own governments
Because history only matters today
Because they have no history before 1900

quizzes.title: Unit 3 Assessment — Spanish Colonial Texas
quizzes.description: This quiz has 12 multiple-choice questions about Unit 3. Choose the best answer for each question. You have 2 tries, and your higher score counts.

questions.text: How was the Spanish colonial government in Texas organized?

answers.text: Local leaders made all their own decisions independently.
The King of Spain held ultimate authority, with power flowing down through the viceroy, governor, and local officials.
Indigenous leaders governed alongside Spanish officials as equal partners.
Colonists elected their own governors through popular vote.

questions.text: What was the role of the Viceroy of New Spain?

answers.text: He commanded the Spanish navy.
He served as the king's representative in the Americas, based in Mexico City.
He was the local governor of Texas.
He led the missions and converted Indigenous peoples.

questions.text: What was the encomienda system?

answers.text: A system for electing colonial leaders.
A trade agreement between Spain and France.
A system that gave Spanish settlers the right to demand labor and tribute from Indigenous peoples.
A method of building missions throughout Texas.

questions.text: How did Spanish trade restrictions affect colonists in Texas?

answers.text: Colonists could only trade with Spain or other Spanish colonies, limiting goods and raising prices.
Colonists could trade freely with anyone.
All trade was completely banned.
Colonists were encouraged to trade with France and England.

questions.text: Which group was most harmed by Spanish colonial policies?

answers.text: Spanish-born officials (peninsulares)
Criollos (American-born Spanish)
Indigenous peoples
French traders

questions.text: What was the Grito de Dolores?

answers.text: A Spanish law banning colonial trade.
Father Miguel Hidalgo's call for Mexican independence in 1810.
A treaty between Spain and France over Texas.
The name of the first Spanish mission in Texas.

questions.text: Who led the final march into Mexico City that completed Mexican independence in 1821?

answers.text: Miguel Hidalgo
José María Morelos
Agustín de Iturbide
Stephen F. Austin

questions.text: What changed for Texas when Mexico became independent from Spain in 1821?

answers.text: Nothing changed — Spain still controlled Texas.
Texas became part of the new nation of Mexico, with new laws and policies.
Texas immediately became its own independent country.
Texas was given to France.

questions.text: How did mission life affect Indigenous peoples' daily routines?

answers.text: The mission system regulated nearly every aspect of daily life, including when to wake, pray, work, and eat.
Indigenous peoples were free to follow their own traditions inside the missions.
Missions only required attendance at Sunday services.
Indigenous peoples ran the missions themselves.

questions.text: What eventually resulted from the unequal effects of Spanish colonial policies?

answers.text: Everyone became satisfied with the system.
Spain gave Indigenous peoples more power.
Resentment grew among criollos and Indigenous peoples, contributing to independence movements.
Spain abandoned all its colonies voluntarily.

questions.text: What is the correct order of authority in Spanish colonial government?

answers.text: King → Council of the Indies → Viceroy → Governor → Local Officials
Governor → Viceroy → King → Council of the Indies
Viceroy → King → Governor → Local Officials
Council of the Indies → King → Viceroy → Governor

questions.text: How did Texas change under Mexican rule compared to Spanish rule?

answers.text: Trade became even more restricted.
Mexico opened Texas to more immigration and offered land grants to attract settlers.
The mission system was expanded with more missions built.
Indigenous peoples gained full control of the government.

quizzes.title: Unit 4 Assessment — Mexican Texas and Colonization
quizzes.description: This quiz has 12 multiple-choice questions about Unit 4. Choose the best answer for each question. You have 2 tries, and your higher score counts.

questions.text: What was an empresario?

answers.text: A person who received a land grant from Mexico and agreed to recruit settlers to Texas.
A Spanish military officer who built forts in Texas.
A Mexican president who opposed immigration to Texas.
A French trader who smuggled goods into Texas.

questions.text: Who were the two most prominent empresarios in Texas?

answers.text: Sam Houston and Davy Crockett
Stephen F. Austin and Martín de León
Santa Anna and Iturbide
William Travis and Jim Bowie

questions.text: What were settlers required to do under the empresario system?

answers.text: Speak only English and follow American laws.
Become Mexican citizens, convert to Catholicism, and be loyal to Mexico.
Pay Spain a yearly tax on their land.
Serve in the Mexican military for five years.

questions.text: Why did settlers choose to build colonies near rivers?

answers.text: Rivers were the only places Mexico allowed settlement.
Rivers provided water for farming, transportation, and drinking water for families and livestock.
Rivers were the easiest places to build forts.
Mexico required all settlements to be on the coast.

questions.text: What was Stephen F. Austin's colony capital?

answers.text: San Antonio
San Felipe de Austin
Nacogdoches
Galveston

questions.text: What crops and goods were most important to the early Texas economy?

answers.text: Gold and silver
Cotton, cattle, and corn
Tobacco and rice
Lumber and furs

questions.text: What did the Law of April 6, 1830 do?

answers.text: It granted more land to American settlers.
It banned further American immigration to Texas and imposed new customs duties.
It made Texas an independent state within Mexico.
It gave empresarios more power over their colonies.

questions.text: Why was the Mexican government concerned about American settlers in Texas?

answers.text: Americans refused to farm the land.
Americans outnumbered Mexican citizens in Texas and maintained American customs and language.
Americans were allied with France against Mexico.
Americans refused to pay for their land grants.

questions.text: What was the Fredonian Rebellion?

answers.text: An early, failed attempt by settlers near Nacogdoches to declare independence from Mexico.
A battle between empresarios Austin and de León.
A Mexican military invasion of Texas.
A trade dispute between Texas and Louisiana.

questions.text: What happened to Stephen F. Austin in Mexico City in 1834?

answers.text: He was elected president of Mexico.
He signed a new empresario contract.
He was arrested and imprisoned for over a year.
He negotiated Texas independence peacefully.

questions.text: What were the Conventions of 1832 and 1833?

answers.text: Military battles between Texians and Mexican troops.
Meetings where Texian settlers listed their grievances and requested reforms from Mexico.
Celebrations of Mexican independence held in Texas.
Trade agreements between Texas and the United States.

questions.text: How did free enterprise work differently in early Texas compared to what Mexico wanted?

answers.text: Texas settlers wanted more government control of trade.
Settlers wanted to trade freely with the U.S. and other countries, but Mexico restricted trade to protect its own economy.
Mexico encouraged unlimited free trade with all nations.
Settlers refused to engage in any trade at all.

quizzes.title: Unit 5 Assessment — Texas Revolution and Independence
quizzes.description: This quiz has 12 multiple-choice questions about Unit 5. Choose the best answer for each question. You have 2 tries, and your higher score counts.

questions.text: What was the significance of the Battle of Gonzales in 1835?

answers.text: It was the final battle of the Texas Revolution.
It was the first military conflict of the Texas Revolution, where Texians refused to return a cannon to Mexico.
It was where the Texas Declaration of Independence was signed.
It was where Santa Anna was captured.

questions.text: What phrase appeared on the flag flown at the Battle of Gonzales?

answers.text: "Remember the Alamo"
"Don't Tread on Me"
"Come and Take It"
"Liberty or Death"

questions.text: Where was the Texas Declaration of Independence signed?

answers.text: San Antonio
Goliad
Washington-on-the-Brazos
San Felipe de Austin

questions.text: How many delegates signed the Texas Declaration of Independence?
How long did the siege of the Alamo last?

answers.text: 3 days
13 days
30 days
1 day

questions.text: Who wrote the famous "Victory or Death" letter from the Alamo?

answers.text: Davy Crockett
Jim Bowie
William Barret Travis
Sam Houston

questions.text: Who was the Tejano leader who served as a defender at the Alamo and later fought at San Jacinto?

answers.text: Martín de León
Juan Seguín
Agustín de Iturbide
Lorenzo de Zavala

questions.text: What was the Runaway Scrape?

answers.text: A Mexican military retreat after the Alamo.
The mass flight of Texas civilians eastward after the fall of the Alamo and the Goliad Massacre.
Sam Houston's surprise attack at San Jacinto.
A nickname for the Battle of Gonzales.

questions.text: How long did the Battle of San Jacinto last?

answers.text: 3 days
Several hours
About 18 minutes
One full week

questions.text: What battle cry did Texian soldiers use at San Jacinto?

answers.text: "Come and Take It!"
"Victory or Death!"
"Remember the Alamo! Remember Goliad!"
"Liberty for Texas!"

questions.text: What happened after the Battle of San Jacinto?

answers.text: Mexico immediately recognized Texas independence.
Santa Anna was captured and signed the Treaties of Velasco, and Texas won its independence as the Republic of Texas.
Texas became a U.S. state right away.
The war continued for another two years.

questions.text: Who became the first elected president of the Republic of Texas?

answers.text: Stephen F. Austin
William Barret Travis
Sam Houston
Mirabeau Lamar
